title: Radical Effort
subtitle: A Bridge Between Here and There
html:
“A journey of a thousand miles begins with your first step… but ends with you collapsing a thousand miles away, prolly in some desert somewhere.” —Dylan MacDonald (Norm MacDonald’s son)

I don’t know if I’m tryin’ to end up in some desert somewhere, but I’m definitely on a journey of a thousand miles, so to speak. I’m overeducated and underemployed, and I need to do something about that. Even with a BS in Computer Science & Neurobiology, an MS in Biomedical Data Science, and a first-author publication in a Q1 journal, my typical interaction with potential employers sounds like your average midwestern night: crickets. I want my journey of a thousand miles to be a journey of creation—willing things into existence that will contribute to the greater good of humanity. But the crickets tell me I’m off track, and that change is in order.

There’s a hidden message in the harmony of stridulation, though. But it’s difficult to make out. Is it that I’m worthless? Incompetent? Stupid? As anyone searching for a job in today’s job market knows, these are common thoughts that we job hunters contend with regularly. But no, that isn’t the message, even if it sure sounds like it sometimes. The message is that we, the applicants—little radio towers trying to send an SOS for an employer to intercept—are not sending strong enough signals. While the amplitude of our signal is, in part, skill-dependent, it is much more a function of our real-world output.

Employers want to see that you have either done the job they need you to do or have the drive and skillset required to learn it. Completing projects in X area gives you a very strong signal along that area’s specific frequency, while documenting your progress signal-boosts you in many directions. They say, “I’m a high agency person. I build things. This is what I’m building.” Being a high-agency builder across any domain is a very strong signal.

But building takes effort.

Radical Effort.

That’s what this publication is about: chronicling my journey of a thousand miles—from jobless to who knows where; maybe in some desert somewhere. I can’t promise outcomes, but I can promise effort.

So here goes nothing.
